newsitem.title: SPAIN: OPINION - Spain Treasury director on bono spread.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Spain Treasury director on bono spread.

text.p: By Jaime Caruana, Spanish Treasury Director

The spectacular reduction in the 10-year spread (to German Bunds) during 1996 and the first months of 1997, which puts the spread at levels near 70 basis points now, basically reflects the great improvement in Spanish economic indicators during the period, that is to say:

- the firm commitment to fulfil the objective of three percent of gross domestic product in the budget deficit of 1997, helped, among other factors, by the reduction in the weight of interest on public debt as a result of lower interest rates.

- the recovery in economic activity, seen in the favourable evolution of employment data -- in the last 12 months the unemployment rate has been reduced by 1.4 percentage points -- as well as by provisional growth data on gross domestic product during the first quarter of the year.

- the backing given by the European Union (EU) to Spain's convergence programme, a reflection of the new economic policy that is being developed by the government with the objective of guaranteeing that Spain is in the group that launches Economic and Monetary Union.
- the stability shown by the peseta in the foreign exchange markets during a relatively long time period.

Markets have reacted favourably to these indicators, increasing considerably the probability awarded the entrance of Spain into Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the first moment and reducing, thereby, the risk premium demanded for our debt.

(NOTE - The opinions expressed in this column represent those of the author only. They should not be seen as representing the views of Reuters. The translation from the Spanish language into English was carried out by Reuters.)
